primitives.meaning: a submission contesting an identifiable prior decision
entryFilters: a submission contesting an identifiable prior decision
no instance of this journey is already open for the the appeal
hard gates (GLB-31) allow communication for this purpose

primitives.does: Link the appeal to the original decision and capture the reason, the evidence submitted, when it arrived and any deadline. The original decision is not modified by an appeal existing against it

primitives.asks: Is the appeal eligible for review?

branches.label: Eligible
branches.test: it contests a reviewable decision, within any applicable window, from someone entitled to contest it

branches.label: Not eligible
branches.test: out of time, not a reviewable decision, or brought by someone with no standing

orderedRoles.eligibleWhen: the message has to be kept and survive until the person can act on it

primitives.purpose: Decline the appeal with the actual reason and whatever process does apply.
primitives.brief: Decline the appeal with the actual reason and whatever process does apply. A rejection that does not say why is the thing that produces the next complaint
primitives.label: CANONICAL_RULE

primitives.state: appeal not eligible; original decision unchanged
primitives.reEntry: a differently grounded appeal, or new evidence, is assessed on its own terms

primitives.asks: Does policy require the original decision to be held while the review runs?

branches.label: Hold required
branches.test: policy suspends the effect of the decision pending review

branches.label: No hold
branches.test: the decision remains in effect during review, which is the default

primitives.does: Suspend the effect of the decision, recorded as a hold rather than as a reversal. Suspended and overturned are different states, and writing one as the other pre-decides the review

primitives.reads: the the appeal re-read from the system of record before acting on the timeout

primitives.on: a review deadline passing without a conclusion
carries: the appeal, the original decision and everything gathered
the fact that no outcome has been reached, so nothing downstream records one

branches.label: MORE_INFORMATION_REQUIRED
branches.test: the review cannot conclude on what it has

primitives.reads: the the appeal re-read from the system of record before acting on the timeout

primitives.does: Update the effective business state to match the conclusion - upheld leaves the decision standing, reversed replaces its effect, modified supersedes it in part. In every case the original decision, the appeal and the review outcome all remain readable; nothing is edited in place, because the record of what was decided and then changed is the point of having an appeal process at all

orderedRoles.eligibleWhen: the message has to be kept and survive until the person can act on it

primitives.purpose: Ask the appellant for the specific evidence the review is missing, naming only what is missing and leaving the appeal deadline where it was.
primitives.brief: Ask the appellant for the specific evidence the review is missing, naming only what is missing and leaving the appeal deadline where it was. Suspending a review for information nobody requested makes the appellant responsible for a gap they were never told about
primitives.label: CANONICAL_RULE

orderedRoles.eligibleWhen: the message has to be kept and survive until the person can act on it

primitives.purpose: State the review's conclusion, which effective state now applies as a result, and what remains available procedurally.
primitives.brief: State the review's conclusion, which effective state now applies as a result, and what remains available procedurally. An appeal that concludes in silence leaves the appellant holding the original decision and no way to know it was reconsidered
primitives.label: CANONICAL_RULE

primitives.state: review concluded; original decision and outcome both preserved
primitives.reEntry: a further appeal, where the process allows one, contests this outcome rather than the original decision
